name: Elizabeth Nyimenka Benson
missingPieces: Stored XSS and path traversal are not in the D1 catalogue itself, though both are fully exploited and quoted in D2 and D3.
feedback: D1 is strong. You catalogue eight of the ten findings with the correct OWASP class, a matching CWE, and a quoted source line each: SQL injection (A03/CWE-89), unsalted MD5 (A02/CWE-916), alg:none (CWE-347), the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), no token expiry (A07/CWE-613), insecure cookie flags (A05/CWE-614), open redirect (A01/CWE-601), and XXE (A05/CWE-611). Your decoy work is exactly what the key wants: you name the tempting hand-rolled HS256 branch and prove it safe at the mechanism level, that hash_equals() is constant-time so the timing-attack worry does not apply and the real bugs live in the alg:none branch and the secret. Where D1 loses ground is that stored XSS and path traversal never appear as catalogue entries here, even though you exploit both later, so two of the ten findings are missing from the table and you spent rows on verbose error disclosure instead. Classing alg:none under A02 rather than A07 is a defensible variant, so I did not penalise it. D2 is excellent. The chain runs in order with every hop reconciled to a capture line, the failed guess at 02:14:55, SQLi at 02:15:31, the 312-row pull at 02:16:04, XSS at 02:18:47, redirect at 02:21:13, file read at 02:24:02, plus the parallel XXE, ending at the exfil sample, with verbatim PoC at each hop. Your CVSS work carries full vectors with justifying sentences, the SQLi at CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N 9.1 matches the key exactly including A:N, and the chained 10.0 with Scope:Changed is argued properly through the file read reaching the signing secret. Your impact figure of roughly 63,000,000 NGN across 312 customers states its assumptions and ties to BoltCash in six weeks, which is what we reward over a bare number. D3 is report-grade: a jargon-free executive summary that lands on customers and naira, a real threat model, findings tied to evidence, the decoy stated correctly, the earliest-break fix named as removing the alg:none branch, remediation ordered by effort-to-risk rather than CVSS severity, and two detection stopgaps with exact fields and false-positive rates. One slip in D3 cost a point: you call the app a Django application in the executive summary and remediation when the recovered source is PHP, so keep the platform consistent with the evidence. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 canons 2 and 3 by number in a load-bearing way, and anchors NDPA 2023 Section 40(3) to the duty to inform the 312 affected data subjects in plain language. This is near-complete work with no fabrication. The single most important fix is to make D1 a complete catalogue: add stored XSS (A03/CWE-79) and path traversal (A01/CWE-22) as their own entries with quoted lines, since a findings catalogue that omits two of the ten you went on to exploit undersells the strongest report you submitted.
